name: Vault DTP

lineage.ref: Tresor, Leipziger Strasse 126a, opened March 1991 in the vault of the ruined Wertheim department store
lineage.why: The room is a strongbox in the death strip and the graphics inherit it: steel, concrete, safe-deposit grids and a name that is just the German word for the room.
A decommissioned electrical substation used as a club. The flyers carry technical furniture — bars, rules, plate numbers — because the building came with them.

lineage.ref: "Tresor II: Berlin & Detroit - A Techno Alliance" (Tresor Records, 1993)
lineage.why: Establishes the Detroit-Berlin axis the whole scene ran on, and the design register that came with it: militant, technical, and printed cheaply on both sides.

lineage.ref: Aldus PageMaker and CorelDRAW on a 486, output to a copy shop laser printer
lineage.why: Stretched and skewed type, hairline rules, drop shadows and outlines exist because those were the buttons. The look is a toolbar, and being honest about that is the position.

lineage.ref: Love Parade flyers and handbills, Danielle de Picciotto and Dr. Motte (Berlin, 1989- )
lineage.why: The handbill as the only distribution channel: no listings magazine would carry it, so the paper had to do all of it — where, when, how much, who is playing.

lineage.ref: East German DTP and the Ocean Club / Raster circle around Frank Bretschneider, early 1990s
lineage.why: A specific post-Wende visual dialect: western software, eastern printers, and no design tradition to be respectful of.

worldview: A flyer is a functional object with a job: get four hundred people to an unmarked door in an industrial building at two in the morning. Everything on it is information — the room, the date, the names, the price — and the design exists to make that information survive being folded into a jacket pocket and read under a streetlight. The vocabulary is whatever the software could do in 1993: flat bars, hairline rules, type stretched past its design width, outlines, repeated blocks. It is not tasteful and does not want to be; taste is a thing clubs get when they start advertising to people who would not otherwise come. Printed one colour on both sides, five thousand at a time, and every one of them ends up on the floor by four a.m.

tensions.and: the flyer is the most collected artefact of the era
tensions.claim: Every claim this position makes about being merely useful is contradicted by the archives, the reprints and the auction prices. The graphics were doing identity work the whole time while insisting they were doing logistics, and the insistence was part of how the identity worked.

tensions.between: the software's defaults produced the look
tensions.and: the look is now chosen deliberately
tensions.claim: Stretched type was what happened when you dragged a corner handle. Choosing it now means choosing the appearance of not having chosen, and that is a different act with the same output. The distinction is invisible in the artefact and decisive about what it means.

tensions.between: the room is a real ruin
tensions.and: the ruin is the selling point
tensions.claim: Tresor was in a vault because the vault was empty and free, in a city with a hole through the middle of it. Industrial imagery attached to a room that is merely styled to look industrial is a description of a marketing decision, not of a building.

tensions.and: the sheet being read in the dark, quickly, once
tensions.claim: Every name on the bill is somebody who will not come if their name is small, and every additional name makes the whole thing less readable. The flyer is always losing this argument and the compromises show, which is most of what it looks like.

commitments.why: Room, date, bill, price. A flyer with fewer than four pieces of text has left one of them off, and the one it left off is the one somebody needed.
Flat filled rectangles: the reverse-out bar, the sidebar, the black block behind the date. Three of them, because that is how a page gets built when the software has no grid.
The rule was the only ornament in the toolbox and it did everything: separated, underlined, filled space, implied a table that was never there.
The signature move is a headline dragged to three hundred percent of its width, skewed fifteen degrees and outlined. This asks for more type instead, which is not the same thing at all.
commitments.blocked_by: a per-text-op or per-glyph transform: `text` takes a size and a tracking on a horizontal baseline, and `transform.scale` is uniform with no skew, so type cannot be stretched, skewed, outlined or set on a curve. The probe's workaround is extrusion, a `repeat` of 96 translated copies of one text op, which smears the word without distorting a single letterform

params.text: Does this describe a specific building, or a genre of building? Look for something that could only be true of one room: a plate number, a floor, an entrance instruction, a fact about the structure. Then look for the failure mode: generic industrial signifiers (rust, chain link, warning stripes, concrete texture) that could be pasted onto any venue in any city. Techno graphics have been recycling the signifiers of a ruin for thirty years; the question is whether there is a ruin.

commitments.why: Specificity of reference is a claim about the world. The tree can be made to contain the word 'vault' and cannot be made to mean it.

params.text: Does this look like it went through a real production chain — laser printer, photocopier, cheap offset on absorbent stock — or like a clean file with degradation applied? Real generation loss is directional and uneven: thin strokes disappear before thick ones, solids fill in at their edges, and small type closes up while large type survives. Applied degradation is uniform across scales. Check the smallest and largest elements and ask whether they have suffered differently.

commitments.why: This medium renders every stroke at full fidelity through the same brush engine, so nothing about production chain is present in the pixels at all.

prohibitions.why: There was no illustrator and no budget for one. The page is built from type and boxes; a drawn figure means somebody was commissioned.
Nothing on this sheet was painted. It was set, boxed and photocopied, and soft media are evidence of a hand that was never near it.
One or two colours on coloured stock, five thousand up. Four including the paper is the ceiling and it is already a more expensive print run than most of these got.
The sheet is small and everything has to be on it, so the marks reach most of it. Total coverage means the type has been swallowed by its own background.

generative_rules.rule: Start from the facts and lay them out in order of who will be angry if they are small. The bill is not a composition, it is a negotiation.
Fill any leftover space with a rule, a bar or a repeated block. Empty space on a flyer means information was left off.
Every element sits inside or on top of a rectangle. If something has no box, give it one; boxes are free and were the only structure the software offered.

constraint.why: Repeated blocks are the house pattern, and two levels is what a 486 and an operator with an evening could actually manage.

generative_rules.rule: Set the room name larger than the artists and the date larger than the room. What people forget is which night it was.
Never centre the whole sheet. One strong left edge, everything hung off it, and one element deliberately breaking out to the right.

cliches: chain link, rust and warning stripes as a background for any club night
a chrome or metallic gradient on the word TECHNO
the Berlin Wall, a Trabant, or the TV tower as a location signifier
'UNDERGROUND' set in a technical face with no underground attached
smiley faces, which are the wrong scene, the wrong country and the wrong decade
a fake barcode or a fake security clearance stamp
distressed type where every letter is distressed identically
the word RAVE in a nineties display face used ironically
an unnecessary drop shadow claimed as a period detail
concrete texture photographs used as a wash behind the bill

meta.temperamentWhy: The flyer exists because the night is worth going to; its severity is service to pleasure, not a verdict against it, so it works from a good mood and gets colder as it tightens.
